decisions.executionNote: Begin smooth elbow-up approach: left toward the cyan car, right toward the right camera. Establish downward tool pitch while maintaining separation.
Continue separated overhead approaches with gradually increased downward pitch. Check wrist alignment before final descent.
Lower slowly toward the car and camera; square left grip to car and rotate right jaws toward the camera's narrow dimension.
Make small visual centering corrections, descend to the objects, and close both grippers. Retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Lift both closed grasps clear of the table, then start toward blue for cars and red for cameras. Verify objects follow the grippers.
Right camera appears retained; carry it over red. Left car did not lift, so reopen and reapproach its new orientation at a lower grasp height.
Release the camera inside red and retract. Left wrist suggests the cyan car is ahead of the pinch center; advance slightly and lower before closing.
Test the cyan-car grasp with a vertical lift, then start toward blue. Right retreats toward the central camera, rotating above the clear table; keep arms separated front-to-back.
Carry the visibly retained cyan car to blue. Keep the right arm clear while orienting its jaws for the red car beneath it before tackling the remaining central camera.
Replan after the guard: use smaller left translations, lower the held car and tilt forward toward blue to avoid excessive elbow flexion. Right descends toward the aligned red car.
Release the cyan car inside blue and withdraw left. Fine-center and lower the right grip onto the red car, then close for a lift test.
Lift-test the red car and start toward the right half of blue. Withdraw the left arm toward the black pen, rotating its jaws above the table.
Carry the retained red car over the right side of blue with a small forward tilt. Lower the left open gripper toward the black pen using wrist-image centering.
The red car appears outside blue after contact at its rim. Back the right arm away and raise it for a new grasp. Continue small left pen-centering corrections.
The previous action was rejected without motion. Hold right orientation, open first, then retreat upward in much smaller increments; continue left's gentle pen approach.
Close on the centered black pen and lift-test it. Reorient right jaws across the red car's narrower dimension while clear of the rim, then begin a cautious descent.
The pen remained on the table after the lift; reopen and descend lower while maintaining its lateral alignment. Right approaches the red car cautiously without pushing farther into the basket.
Hold the pen closed and lift to check retention. Close the right grip around the red car, then lift vertically clear of the basket rim before attempting transport again.
Both objects visibly follow the grips. Carry the pen toward white. Shift the red car inward over blue while tilting forward to increase rim clearance without further large elbow flexion.
Replan from the accepted prefix: lower the right wrist while tilting the held car forward over blue, avoiding further elbow over-flexion. Advance the pen over white.
No motion occurred on the rejected action. Halve right translation and rotation increments to move away smoothly from its highly flexed configuration; continue pen placement.
Move the red car inward and forward over blue now that the right elbow has more margin. The pen appears to hang near the front rim; lift it before advancing farther.
Release the red car within blue, then retreat gently from the flexion boundary. The black pen has fallen outside white; withdraw the open left grip to recover it.
Both cars now appear inside blue. Reorient left above the fallen pen and bring right toward the remaining central camera, keeping the arms laterally separated and away from basket rims.
Center the pen and camera from the wrist views while descending in small increments. Align right jaws across the camera's short dimension; defer closing until final visual check.
Shift the left pinch from the pen tip toward its barrel and lower slightly. Lower the centered camera grip, close both, then verify retention in the next lift.
Lift both closed grasps, moving the camera back into the right workspace. Begin a slight forward tilt only after clearing the tabletop; check both objects remain retained.
Both objects remain visible in the grips. Carry the pen well inside white and the camera toward red, tilting forward gradually to preserve elbow-up reach margin.
Set the second camera fully inside red and open. The pen slipped outside white during transport; retreat and reorient for a barrel-centered grasp without subsequent tilting.
Cameras are released together in red. Recenter the black pen's barrel and descend left; withdraw right toward the white pen and align jaws perpendicular to its length.
Continue small wrist-guided corrections: bring the black pen between the left jaws and lower; shift right toward the white pen's barrel while descending, without closing yet.
Left approach is obstructed by the basket rim; stop pressing downward and test a stationary close followed by a vertical lift. Center and lower right onto the white pen, then close.
Reapproach the black pen with a narrow opening to clear the basket wall and shift from its tip toward the barrel. Lift the white pen and start toward a central staging spot for left-arm pickup.
Narrow the left opening further and correct toward the black barrel before a gentle close-and-lift test. Carry the white pen to a central staging area, keeping the right arm on its own side.
Lift-test the black pen without rotating it. Lower the retained white pen onto the central clear tabletop for a sequential left-arm pickup; do not cross the arms.
Release the white pen on the clear central table and withdraw right. The black pen remains against the basket; move left toward an unoccupied section of the front rim to create grasp clearance.
Approach the empty white basket's front-right wall below the rim with closed left fingers, away from the black pen. Park right clear of the central staged pen.
The basket wall resists motion, so stop pushing it. Bring closed left tips over the black pen to attempt a gentle roll away from the wall. Begin restoring right's home orientation in clear space.
Withdraw the closed left tips along the tabletop to try rolling the black pen away from the basket, without further pressure into the wall. Continue a smooth right-arm return toward home.
The black pen remains beside the wall. Lift clear and turn the closed left fingers to present a narrower profile for moving it away. Finish the right-arm home approach.
Replan after the orientation limit: no further left yaw. Lower the narrow closed fingers toward the pen's wall side for a gentle outward roll; settle right at home.
Correct the rejected tensor; no motion occurred. Place the closed left tips just behind the black barrel, then sweep gently away from the basket. Right stays still and open.
Previous sweep appears above the barrel. Lower the closed tips cautiously to the pen's wall side, then make a short outward sweep, monitoring for obstruction.
The basket obstructs the vertical approach. Withdraw upward and backward, opening and reorienting for an angled approach from the clear table side rather than pressing into the wall.
Use the angled tool to reach the barrel from in front of the basket, keeping the palm farther from the wall. Descend with a narrow opening and inspect before closing.
Make a small wrist-guided correction away from the wall, lower to barrel height, close, and test a short upward-and-backward lift without changing orientation.
The prior close missed the barrel. Shift along the pen toward its middle with the angled palm clear of the basket, lower slightly, and close again.
Lift the closed left grip up and away from the basket without rotating, to distinguish a retained pen from another missed close. Right remains parked open.
The pen did not follow the lift. Reapproach farther along the barrel and lower the angled jaws, leaving them open for an alignment check before closing.
The barrel now lies between the open fingers but slightly past the pinch center. Make a small longitudinal correction, close, and lift vertically without changing orientation.
The pen stayed on the table. Recenter left slightly along the barrel and approach deeper from the clear side with open jaws; keep the basket and both completed groups undisturbed.
Close at the current barrel alignment, pause, then lift away from the wall without rotating. Check whether the pen actually follows before transporting it.
The black pen shifted relative to the grip rather than staying retained. Recenter on its new barrel position and approach lower from the clear side before closing.
Test this deeper grasp by lifting slowly upward and away from the basket, keeping the left orientation fixed and the grip closed.
The pen is now slightly clear of the wall but not retained. Reorient above it to make both jaws level with the table; this avoids one finger contacting the table before the other reaches the barrel.
With level jaws, the wrist view shows the barrel well left and ahead of the pinch center. Correct that offset while descending, keeping a moderate opening to clear the basket.
Correct the small remaining barrel offset with level jaws and a narrower opening; lower to pinch height and close without rotating.
Lift the closed, level-jaw grasp slowly without rotating, moving slightly away from the wall to verify whether the black pen follows.
The pen now appears to follow the grip. Raise it above the rim and shift inward so its long overhanging end fits within white; introduce only a gentle forward tilt.
The black pen is retained above white. Advance it fully past the front wall, lower slightly, and release inside while the right arm remains parked.
Withdraw from white after releasing the black pen. Approach the staged white pen from the left, restoring level downward jaws while the right arm stays home.
Move the open left grip over the staged white pen, stopping just left of the centerline. Maintain level jaws and inspect alignment before final descent.
The white pen's tip is near the pinch center but its barrel lies farther along the tool-camera view. Shift toward the barrel and descend, keeping ample separation from the parked right arm.
Center the white barrel between level jaws, descend the final small distance, close, and begin a short vertical retention test.
Lift the white pen clear of the table, then begin transport back into the left workspace toward white. Keep closed and verify retention before crossing the basket rim.
The white pen remains retained. Carry it toward white at rim-clearing height, with its overhanging tip kept inside the basket's lateral bounds.
Advance the retained white pen fully inside white, lower gently, and release beside the black pen. Pause to let it settle before withdrawing.
All three categories appear separated and released. Withdraw left clear of white and begin a continuous elbow-up return to origin; correct the small right-home residual.
Continue returning the open left arm along a clear elevated path, gradually restoring home orientation while preserving joint continuity. Objects remain settled in their category baskets.
Ease left toward origin with a curved, slowing approach rather than a final large joint change. Keep both grippers open and leave the sorted objects undisturbed.
